subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that (tan θ + sec θ − 1)/(tan θ − sec θ + 1) = (1 + sin θ)/cos θ.

mark_split.label: Cancel and write in sin and cos

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 40, book p.93. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards the substitution 1 = sec²θ − tan²θ and the factoring it makes possible first, and the cancellation plus the change to sin and cos second. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations holds two of those ten slots. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Checked numerically at θ = 40°, 100°, 200° and 320°: the two sides agree to ten decimal places (2.1445069205, −11.4300523028, −0.7002075382 and 0.4663076582). The denominator tan θ − sec θ + 1 is zero exactly when sin θ + cos θ = 1, and with cos θ ≠ 0 that means θ = 2nπ; at θ = 0 it computes to 0.0000000000, which is why that family of angles is excluded on the page and not only here.

recall_prompt: Say what you would put in place of the 1 in the numerator, and say how the proof finishes.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Replace 1 by sec²θ − tan²θ
steps.margin_note: First mark. The −1 is the obstacle. Writing it as sec²θ − tan²θ makes every term carry the factor sec θ + tan θ, and the bracket left over is the denominator itself.
steps.memory_tip: Replace the 1 with sec²θ − tan²θ. The numerator then carries the whole denominator as a factor.
lines: tan θ and sec θ appear, so cos θ ≠ 0.
Also tan θ − sec θ + 1 ≠ 0; it is 0 when
sin θ + cos θ = 1, that is at θ = 2nπ.
In the numerator put 1 = sec²θ − tan²θ:
= (sec θ + tan θ)[1 − (sec θ − tan θ)]
= (sec θ + tan θ)(tan θ − sec θ + 1)

recall.must_convey: That 1 is written as sec²θ − tan²θ, and the numerator then factors as (sec θ + tan θ)(tan θ − sec θ + 1).
accept: write one as sec squared theta minus tan squared theta in the numerator
then sec theta plus tan theta comes out as a common factor
the numerator becomes sec theta plus tan theta times the denominator
one ni sec square minus tan square ga rasi common factor teestam
use the identity for one so the numerator factorises
reject: one plus sin theta by cos theta

steps.why: The −1 is the obstacle. Replacing it with sec²θ − tan²θ makes both terms of the numerator carry the factor sec θ + tan θ, and the bracket that is left is exactly the denominator, so the fraction is about to collapse.
common_mistakes: Replacing 1 by sin²θ + cos²θ, which does not factor here.
Forgetting that the denominator must not be 0.

steps.label: Cancel and write in sin and cos
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The whole denominator is a factor of the numerator, so the fraction is sec θ + tan θ, and that is (1 + sin θ)/cos θ.
steps.memory_tip: After the factoring the fraction is simply sec θ + tan θ, and sec θ + tan θ = (1 + sin θ)/cos θ.
lines: The denominator is not 0, so it cancels:

recall.must_convey: That the denominator cancels leaving sec θ + tan θ, which equals (1 + sin θ)/cos θ.
accept: the denominator cancels so what is left is sec theta plus tan theta
sec theta plus tan theta is one over cos plus sin over cos which is one plus sin theta by cos theta
cancel the common bracket and convert to sin and cos
denominator cancel avutundi, sec theta plus tan theta migulutundi
write both in terms of cos theta and add
reject: write one as sec squared minus tan squared

steps.why: The whole denominator is a factor of the numerator, so the quotient is just sec θ + tan θ. Writing both of those over the common denominator cos θ gives the right side directly.
common_mistakes: Cancelling before the numerator has been factored.
Writing sec θ + tan θ as (1 + cos θ)/sin θ.
